newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia has full order books for wheat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia has full order books for wheat.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board has full orders for months ahead and is unable to sell more wheat in nearby months, chairman Trevor Flugge said on Wednesday.

"I won't say we're knocking back sales but we are just logistically not able to sell any more wheat in the nearby months," he said after an address to the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) outlook conference.
"We would like to and as much as some people would like to buy, the logistics at ports just won't allow us to do it," Flugge said. "We are certainly in the best possible position."
The AWB had not sold out of Australian Standard White (ASW) but had reached the point where it had sold enough that it was now looking at the quality end of the market, he said.
This put the AWB in a good position for May to September when it would be competing with North American wheat on world markets, he added.
Flugge also said that prices the AWB had been able to demand and extract on world markets were higher than would be the case if it had plenty of positions open.
On pricing, Flugge said the AWB was faced with the choice of discounting by up to A$30.00 a tonne on export markets in October and November.
But it had refrained from becoming particularly aggressive and had seen no need to "jump in and throw wheat away," he said.
The AWB's decision not to discount had now been vindicated, he said.
Flugge also said he believed Australia was heading for a 1997/98 wheat crop of about 17.2 million tonnes, down from the current record crop of 23 million tonnes.
The chances were low of Australia having a repeat of the current year's favourable weather, he said.
